text: Anybody can sense a signal, right? So if this user, let's call it B, transmits something toward the access point, B and C, the other user nodes. In this scenario that we are assuming, we'll be able to sense that there is a signal on the channel because they can hear each other. Okay, so you understand the difference between the fact that a user can only communicate with the access point, but he can hear everybody else. Communicating and hearing, hearing are two different things. Communicating means that you have established a communication link between two nodes, and that you can transfer packets from one node to the other. That's what we have between each user node and the access point. Okay, but hearing is just the ability to sense, okay, that there is a signal. But you are not going to demodulate the payload of packets that are sent by other user nodes. Okay, because those packets cannot be for you. They can only be for the access point.
